sources.title: Hurricane Beryl 2024: Global Rapid Post-Disaster Damage Estimation (GRADE) Report
sources.organization: World Bank Group and Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery
sources.temporal_coverage: Rapid direct-damage assessment following Hurricane Beryl on 1 July 2024; report as of 26 July 2024.
sources.methodology: Rapid engineering-based damage estimation using reported assessments, exposure data, satellite imagery and modeled wind fields.
sources.limitations: Preliminary rapid estimates; damage to buildings on Saint Vincent was not disaggregated by census division or damage level.

sources.title: National Climate Change Policy of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
sources.organization: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; prepared with technical assistance from CANARI
sources.temporal_coverage: Policy priority period 2018–2030; vulnerability narrative draws on historical events and farmer observations through 2019.
sources.methodology: Government policy document informed by literature, climate modeling and three rounds of stakeholder consultation during 2018–2019.
sources.limitations: The document mixes historical observations with policy priorities; stated actions are not evidence of implementation or current outcomes.

sources.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on the Path to Recovery with support from UNDP, Canada and CDEMA
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Barbados and the Eastern Caribbean
sources.temporal_coverage: Post-Beryl recovery activities, including workshops in November 2025 and March 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP news account of partner-supported post-disaster training and school-equipment activities.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; the page provides no independent evaluation of preparedness or resilience effects.

sources.title: Building Resilience with Frontier Technology: Union Island’s 3D Printing and Design Capacity Building
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Accelerator Lab, Barbados and the Eastern Caribbean
sources.temporal_coverage: Workshop and printer handover in November 2025; blog published 16 December 2025.
sources.methodology: UNDP Accelerator Lab account of a local design-and-fabrication workshop and stakeholder engagement.
sources.limitations: This is a programme blog; intended local-use cases are not evidence of tested emergency response or measured climate outcomes.

claims.locator: Printed p. 10, section 1.4 ‘Reported impacts’, and Table 3.
claims.paraphrase: Beryl brought Category 3–4 winds to the Southern Grenadines; building damage was extreme on Union Island, extremely severe on Mayreau, severe on Canouan and much lower on Bequia and Mustique.
claims.limitations: Building damage assessments were rapid and preliminary; the report notes approximately 600 damaged buildings on Saint Vincent were not locally disaggregated.

claims.paraphrase: On Union Island, Beryl damaged the hospital, water network, power plant, airport and nearly all berthing structures; on Palm Island it damaged a desalination plant, while Mayreau suffered major structural and communications damage.
claims.limitations: The report draws on rapid surveys and cited partner assessments; it does not quantify duration of service loss at each facility.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 18–20, sections 4.0 ‘Interpretation of results’ and damage summaries.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment estimated US$230.6 million in direct physical damage, about 22% of 2023 GDP; the Southern Grenadines accounted for US$186.8 million, or 81% of the national total.
claims.limitations: These are rapid modeled direct-damage estimates, not household losses or a measure of recovery progress.

claims.locator: Printed p. 8, section 2, paragraph on coastal and Grenadines vulnerability.
claims.paraphrase: The 2019 policy identifies low-lying Grenadines coralline islets as exposed to sea-level rise and storm surge, with coral-bleaching risk to Tobago Cays; lower rainfall also contributes to drought and saltwater-intrusion pressure.
institutions: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
claims.limitations: The policy is dated 2019 and presents a vulnerability assessment, not a current measurement of local exposure.

claims.locator: Printed p. 18, agriculture adaptation section, paragraphs on farm slopes and local farmer observations.
claims.paraphrase: The policy describes small farms on slopes often above 30 degrees and reports that cultivation practices on these slopes contribute to landslides during heavy rain; local farmers also noted longer dry periods and more intense rainfall.
claims.limitations: Farmer observations are recorded in a 2019 policy; the passage does not establish event-level attribution or incidence rates.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 18–19, adaptation priorities and energy actions for the Grenadines.
claims.paraphrase: The policy sets adaptation priorities for vulnerable populations and proposes stronger participatory planning, climate information and monitoring, and Grenadines microgrids using solar, wind and battery storage.
institutions: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
claims.limitations: These are policy objectives and proposed actions, not evidence that the measures were implemented.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on the November 2025 school-safety workshop in Union Island.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports a two-day disaster-management and school-safety workshop at the Tobago Cays Marine Park office for teachers and disaster-committee members from Union Island and Mayreau.
claims.limitations: The page reports delivery of training but does not measure subsequent preparedness or response performance.

claims.locator: Article paragraph listing five recipient schools and the equipment handover.
claims.paraphrase: The programme reports EC$385,000 of equipment supplied to Paget Farm Primary, Mayreau Primary, Union Island Secondary, Stephanie Browne Primary and Mary Hutchinson Primary.
institutions: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
claims.limitations: The article lists goods and value but does not assess school functionality or learning outcomes.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on the March 2026 Post-Disaster Needs Assessment training.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports that 32 government and statutory-body staff were trained in post-disaster damage and needs assessment, with housing as the focus because it was the most damaged sector in Beryl.
institutions: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
claims.limitations: Training participation is reported; no later assessment quality or recovery-allocation effect is provided.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on the November 2025 workshop, partners and handover.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports that 20 Union Island students, educators, community members and entrepreneurs took part in hands-on design and fabrication training; a 3D printer was handed to Union Island Secondary School.
claims.limitations: The blog reports workshop attendance and equipment handover, not proven response capability or resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: Article section ‘Why 3D Printing? A Tool for Resilience and Recovery’.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP says Beryl-related isolation and disrupted supply chains can delay imported parts; the workshop presented local fabrication of water-pipe connectors and fishing-gear parts as possible emergency uses.
claims.limitations: This is a proposed use described in a programme blog; no emergency deployment or climate-adaptation benefit is documented.

search_audit.outcome: No inspected source establishes a climate-to-violence or conflict pathway. Sources describe cyclone and drought vulnerability without inferring conflict.

search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documents violence blocking climate adaptation. The World Bank reports hurricane damage and the UNDP pages describe post-disaster supply-chain isolation and local recovery activities.

search_audit.outcome: Directly read UNDP pages document local school/disaster training, equipment handovers and a Union Island design/fabrication workshop. The separate water-resilience and small-grants project pages could not be opened.

gaps: No inspected source establishes a climate-conflict or violence-to-adaptation pathway in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; none is inferred.
The GRADE report is a rapid July 2024 estimate; approximately 600 damaged buildings on Saint Vincent were not disaggregated locally, and some island damage data were preliminary.
The government climate-policy vulnerability evidence dates mainly through 2019; its proposed adaptation measures are not implementation results.
UNDP reports local training and handovers but provides no independent evaluation of response performance or resilience outcomes.
The UNDP Water for Resilience and Union Island small-grants project pages could not be read directly; no search-indexed findings were used.
A World Bank project appraisal document was excluded from findings because it is marked FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, despite public hosting.
